label: If y does not depend for its being on x, then y can be without x
paraphrase: OPEN unrestricted analyst bridge: if y does not depend for its being on x, then y can be without x. It is not valid merely from DEF-DEPENDS-FOR-BEING and DEF-CAN-BE-WITHOUT: if x is necessary, y may be independent of x although no world has y without x. The existing Lean theorem uses this as an explicit conditional premise, not as a derived fact. Restricting x to contingent beings avoids that counterexample but still needs a substantive bridge between counterfactual nondependence and modal separability; it cannot derive unrestricted priority without covering necessary effects.
